text.p: WCE canola and grain futures pre-opening call as of 0845 CDT.

CANOLA - C$1.20 to C$1.50 a tonne lower, following expected losses in CBOT futures. USDA supply and demand data bearish for new crop. USDA raised new crop ending soybean stocks to 285 million bushels. But soyoil ending stocks cut may prompt crusher support under the market. Canada's dollar opened firm at C$1.3689, rose to 82.98 yen, firmed to 1.2856 marks.
FLAXSEED - Down C$0.50. Contract lows expected. Weak export demand, poor crush margins and hedge pressure expected.

WESTERN BARLEY - C$0.50 lower. New contract lows expected on bearishly construed USDA wheat production figures. USDA put U.S. winter wheat production at 1.781 billion bushels, above expectations for 1.687 billion.
FEED WHEAT - C$0.50 down, following USDA wheat production data. Commercial scale down buying seen limiting losses.
PEAS - Mixed. Traders said losses were overdone on Thursday in Oct/Dec, other months seen lagging.
(All values in Canadian dollars/tonne except peas, oats)
